reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the rendered redline is identical to the original with no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited Section 15.2(a) gives our party (Sanofi, the customer/licensee) exactly the preferred carve-outs: assignment to any Affiliate without RevMed consent and assignment in whole, without consent, to a successor/purchaser in a sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or a merger/acquisition. The deterministic check confirms the successor/affiliate carve-out is present.

Vendor-side restrictions are present and directionally favourable to us: RevMed needs our consent (not unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned) for affiliate assignments and may not transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without our consent (15.2(b)).

No RevMed right is triggered by a Change of Control of our party — the cited change-of-control mechanics (p0489) run only on RevMed's Change of Control and confer the option (terminate or elect the alternative) on us, so the walk-away trigger (vendor termination/re-pricing on Customer CoC) is absent.

RevMed's ability to assign in whole on its own Change of Control without our consent, and the absence of an express 'never to a competitor' bar, fall short of preferred but sit at or above the mutual-successor-assignment fallback and are correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.

The residual points flagged in the rationale (post-termination royalty ending on our Change of Control under 12.3(c); withholding gross-up allocation in 9.7(a)) are financial-terms sub-elements rather than assignment restrictions, and are appropriately noted, not raised as a deviation under ASSIGN.
